targets.authors: Tucker MA, Taylor K, Merchant R, et al.
targets.title: Scopolamine does not impact declarative and motor memory consolidation across a night of sleep or a day of wakefulness.
targets.outcome_quote: In the present study, we observed a similar positive correlation between intrinsic motivation and training and retest performance. However, motivation did not correlate with memory consolidation (change in performance from training to retest), nor did intrinsic motivation favor performance in the sleep (v. wake) participants.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The separately hypothesized re-test of a published intrinsic-motivation finding agrees on acquisition but explicitly differs on consolidation.

reasoning: Title, DOI and four authors match; complete methods, results, discussion and reference list inspected. Both Ellenbogen papers are explicitly identified as the basis of this replication. The secondary intrinsic-motivation hypothesis also re-tests published findings from Tucker et al. (2018); other cited sleep studies and motivation measures are background or materials sources.
